clue.text: Cross put back nearly damaged element

indicators.note: put back means the word for cross is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: the cross sign + is a plus

indicators.note: nearly means the word for damaged loses its final letter

parts.note: damaged means hurt

explanation.surface: Someone's cross, pushed back into place, has been almost ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses PLUS to SULP; 'nearly' trims HURT to HUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulphur is a chemical element, atomic number 16, spelt this way in British usage.

clue.text: Dry old PM (not North) quit

parts.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine

indicators.note: not means the letter for North is left out

parts.note: Anthony Eden, British Prime Minister 1955-57

explanation.surface: A dull former prime minister, not from the North, resigned.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to withdraw formally from a union, to quit it.

clue.text: Laughing out loud about article in woolly extract

indicators.note: about means the textspeak abbreviation goes round the article

parts.note: LOL is textspeak for laughing out loud
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone laughs aloud at a magazine piece about wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the grease extracted from sheep's wool.

clue.text: Under Henry I, archery revised pecking order

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, puts the rearranged word below the preceding letters

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, unit of inductance

indicators.note: revised means the letters of archery are rearranged

explanation.surface: Under King Henry the First, archery was reorganised into a strict ranking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry I' looks like the king; it is H and I with ARCHERY rearranged below.
explanation.definitionFit: A pecking order, like a hierarchy, is a ranking of status.

clue.text: Old-fashioned, to bring up young primarily to keep fighting

indicators.note: to keep means the letters hold the word for fighting inside them

parts.note: to rear a child is to bring it up
action means fighting, as in seeing action

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of young

explanation.surface: It's old-fashioned to raise youngsters chiefly to keep fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactionary opposes change and wants old ways restored.

clue.text: Piccard finally cracks two ways to secure source of hot air

indicators.note: cracks means the letter breaks into the middle of the pair of words

parts.note: to win something and to bag it are two ways of securing it

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the name Piccard

parts.note: Auguste Piccard, the Swiss balloonist, or Jean-Luc Picard's namesake; only his final letter is used

explanation.surface: The balloonist Piccard finally lands two ways of securing a supply of hot air for his balloon.
explanation.walkthrough: Auguste Piccard was a pioneering balloonist, which makes 'hot air' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A windbag talks endlessly and emptily, so is figuratively a source of hot air.

clue.text: Wrong sorts of whiskey last to go

indicators.note: last to go means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: W is whiskey in the phonetic alphabet, and rye is a sort of whiskey

explanation.surface: The wrong kinds of whiskey were drunk last.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of whiskey: W from the radio alphabet and RYE, the spirit, together WRYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wry once meant twisted or turned awry, hence wrong or perverse.

clue.text: Homes built in spring succeeded in goals

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the goals

parts.note: in football the nets are the goals
S is short for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Houses built in spring succeeded in reaching their targets.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds build nests in spring as homes for their young.

clue.text: Don't go to expert to cover new floor

indicators.note: to cover means the word for expert wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast expert
to floor someone is to knock them out, KO

explanation.surface: Skip the expert you'd hire to lay a new floor.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNK OFF is British slang for skipping school or work.
explanation.definitionFit: To bunk off is to skip, not attend, school or work.

clue.text: Pledge attempt to seize duke's equipment

indicators.note: to seize means the pledge word grabs the letter inside

parts.note: a gage is something given as a pledge
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A promise to try to take a duke's gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadgetry is a collection of gadgets, mechanical equipment.

clue.text: Church conservators never hosting Eastern anniversary

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: hosting means the run of letters takes another letter inside it

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, which conserves British heritage
nary is a dialect word for never or not one

explanation.surface: Church conservationists never put on an Eastern-themed anniversary.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that conserves historic buildings; 'hosting' puts E inside the run of conservators-plus-never, right after the trust's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A centenary is a hundredth anniversary.

clue.text: Clerical group mired in controversy, no doubt

indicators.note: mired in says the answer is stuck inside the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A church body is bogged down in a dispute, unsurprisingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy governing church affairs.

clue.text: English officer opening US lawman's letter

indicators.note: opening means these letters split the lawman's abbreviation and sit inside it

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor
LT is short for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An English officer opens an American prosecutor's mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, and D in the phonetic alphabet.

clue.text: Grave scene of western battle

definitions.meaning: ..., Arizona, saw the Gunfight at the OK Corral

explanation.surface: A solemn setting for a shootout in a cowboy film.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombstone is a grave marker; Tombstone is the Wild West town of the famous gunfight.

clue.text: Records timber that may be rare

parts.note: minutes are records of a meeting
teak is a hardwood timber

explanation.surface: Records of timber that could be scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' suggests scarce, but it is how a steak is cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute steak is a thin steak cooked briefly, often served rare.

clue.text: Missing curate found on ground outside front of chapel

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters wrap round the single letter
ground, as in crushed, means the letters are broken up and rearranged
front of picks the first letter of chapel

explanation.surface: A curate has gone missing and is later found on the land outside the chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is the anagram signal, not the land; the rearranged CURATE FOUND ON wraps round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unaccounted for has not been traced or explained, so is missing.

clue.text: Odd pie chart at end of cursory study of inscriptions

indicators.note: odd means the letters of pie are set in a strange order

parts.note: a graph is a chart

indicators.note: at end of picks the final letter of cursory

explanation.surface: A strange pie chart concludes a hasty study of inscriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Epigraphy is the scholarly study of ancient inscriptions.

clue.text: They offer covert views of mole on parts of course

parts.note: a mole is a spy
a golf course is made up of holes

explanation.surface: Molehills on the course give secret views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' looks like the animal digging the course; it is a secret agent, and the course is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Spyholes are peepholes giving a hidden view.

clue.text: Stove, frying pans, then old bikes

indicators.note: stove is the past tense of stave, smashed in, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A kitchen list: stove, frying pans, and then, oddly, some old bicycles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stove' looks like a cooker in a kitchen list; it is the past tense of stave (stave in), the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny-farthings were Victorian bicycles with a huge front wheel and tiny rear one.

clue.text: No energy inspires pit candidate

indicators.note: inspires, as in breathing in, means the letters take the word for pit inside

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
a mine is a pit

explanation.surface: A lack of energy inspires a coal-pit candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a candidate put forward for a post.

clue.text: Parisian is probing hole? Ring police

indicators.note: probing means the French word goes inside the word for hole

parts.note: a gap is a hole
est is French for is
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A Parisian is examining a hole and decides to phone the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret police of Nazi Germany.

clue.text: The Woman in White garners Grand Cross

indicators.note: garners means the word for the woman gathers the letter inside

parts.note: a bride traditionally wears white; also the title of a Wilkie Collins novel
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Wilkie Collins's novel wins a grand prize cross.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridge a river is to cross it.

clue.text: One person from Far East owns clothes range

indicators.note: clothes, as a verb, means wraps round, so the letters go inside

parts.note: owns means has
one is the Roman numeral I
a Malay is a person from Malaysia

explanation.surface: One Far Eastern person owns a range of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' reads as a noun but is a verb: HAS clothes I MALAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayas are the great mountain range of Asia.

clue.text: Bond grabs one extended rest

indicators.note: grabs means the word for bond takes the letter inside

parts.note: a lien is a legal claim or bond on property
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: James Bond grabs someone for a long rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is a long rest in bed in the morning.

clue.text: Republican is meeting HM? That's certainly a step up!

parts.note: Her Majesty is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A republican meeting the Queen would be a social step up indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is the vertical board of a stair, the bit you step up over.

clue.text: Left expert holding knight's weapon

indicators.note: holding means the word for expert takes a letter inside

parts.note: an ace is an expert
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A left-handed expert grips a knight's weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by mounted knights in jousting.

clue.text: Chimney cleaner had to cover tip of chin and part of face

parts.note: a sweep cleans chimneys

indicators.note: to cover means the word had is wrapped round the letter
tip of here means the far end, so the last letter of chin is picked

explanation.surface: A sooty chimney sweep had to cover his chin and part of his face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' suggests a human face; it is a clock face.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep hand is the long seconds hand moving round a clock face.

clue.text: Problem with German missing top meeting

indicators.note: missing means the German word is taken away

parts.note: a summit is a meeting of top leaders
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A problem with the German absent from a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is an arithmetic problem, as set in school.

clue.text: A few mentioned pinching diver's bone

indicators.note: pinching means the word sounding like some grabs the bird inside
mentioned says the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a few means some
terns are seabirds that dive for fish

explanation.surface: A few people said they had stolen a diver's bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone.

clue.text: Major books hoarded by economist briefly

indicators.note: hoarded by means the books are stored inside the economist's shortened name
briefly means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: John Maynard Keynes, the economist
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Major books were stockpiled by an economist, in short.
explanation.definitionFit: Keynote, used adjectivally as in keynote speech, means principal or major.
